title: Metering Service Training Note: The Free Test Allowance Belongs to the Agreement
content:
The free-test allowance of the **Metering Service** belongs to the service agreement, not to a single meter.

## The rule

Customer-requested tests on every installation of the same service agreement count together, so exchanging a meter after a test does not renew the allowance. Tests at different service agreements of the same customer are counted separately. Periodic, utility-initiated and Commission referee tests never count toward the allowance.

**What is counted.** For a test under review, the count is the number of test requests with the reason "customer request" recorded on any meter installation of the same service agreement whose request date falls in the window: the meter type's free-test period, in calendar months, ending the day before the request date of the test under review. The test under review is therefore not part of its own count.

## Questions this rule answers

**Does a new meter come with a new free test?** No. Customer-requested tests on the removed meter and on the new meter of the same agreement are counted together.

**Does a test at the customer's other address use up this agreement's allowance?** No. Each service agreement is counted on its own.

**Do company-scheduled tests use the allowance?** No. Periodic, utility-initiated and Commission referee tests are never counted.

## Worked count (hypothetical dates, 12-month free-test period)

A customer-requested test is requested on 15 March 2025. The window runs from 15 March 2024 to 14 March 2025.

| Earlier request on the same agreement | Counted? |
|---|---|
| Customer request on 20 May 2024, on the meter since exchanged | Yes |
| Periodic test request on 1 August 2024 | No (periodic) |
| Customer request on 10 March 2024 | No (before the window) |
| Customer request on 2 January 2025 at the customer's other agreement | No (different agreement) |

The count for the 15 March 2025 test is 1.
